Root / lemma: te/ct^- 

Meaning: to plait; woodwork; carpenter 

Material: Old Indie taksat/ ^behaut, bearbeitet, zimmert, verfertigt', lengthened grade tast/ 

ds., participle tasfa-, common Old Indie -gh- > -ks- : Avestan -gh- > -xs-, -s- Avestan fasta- 

69
temp-
a. Latin téla, web, net, warp of a fabric, also weaver’s beam (to which the warp threads are tied): TILLER?, ToiL2; b. Latin subtilis, thin, fine, precise, subtle (< *sub-téla, “thread passing under the warp,” the finest thread; sub, under; see upo): SUBTLE. 3. Suffixed form *teks-On, weaver, maker of wattle for house walls, builder (possibly contaminated with *teks-tdr, builder), in Greek tekton, carpenter, builder: TECTONIC; ARCHITECT. 4. Suf- fixed form *teks-nd-, craft (of weaving or fabricating), in Greek tekhné, art, craft, skill: TECHNICAL, POLYTECHNIC, TECHNOLOGY. 5. Possibly Germanic *thahsu-, badger (“the animal that builds,” referring to its burrowing skill), in Old High German dahs (> German Dachs), badger but more likely borrowed from the same pre- Indo-European source as the Celtic totemic name Tazgo-, Gaelic Tadhg, “‘badger’”): DACHSHUND. [Pok. tekth- 1058.] tekv-. To run, flee. Suffixed o-grade form *tokv-so- in Iranian *taxsa-, bow, borrowed into Greek toxon, bow, also (in the plural) bow and arrow (< “that which flies’): Toxic. [Pok. tekz- 1059.] tel-. Ground, floor, board. 1. Germanic *thil-j6- in Middle Low German and Middle Dutch dele, plank: DEAL?. 2. Suffixed form *tel-n- in Latin telliis (stem telliir-), earth, the earth: (TELLURIAN), (TELLURIC), (TELLURION), (TELLURIUM), TELLURO-. 3. Possibly reduplicated form *ti-tel- in Latin titulus, placard, label, superscription, title: TITLE. [Pok. 2. tel- 1061.] tela-. To lift, support, weigh; with derivatives referring to measured weights and thence to money and payment. 1. Suffixed form *telo-mon- in Greek telamén, supporter, bearer: TELAMON. 2. Suffixed form *tel/a)-es- in: a. Greek telos, tax, charge: TOLL!; PHILATELY; b. Latin tolerdre, to bear, endure: TOLERATE. 3. Suffixed zero-grade form *th-i-, becoming *tali- (influenced by ¢dlis, such), in Latin ¢alid, reciprocal punishment in kind, “something paid out”: TALION; RETALIATE. 4. Suffixed variant zero-grade form *tala-nt- in Greek talanton, balance, weight, any of several specific weights of gold or silver, hence the sum of money represented by such a weight: TALENT. 5. Perhaps intensive reduplicated form *tantal- in Greek Tantalos, name of a legendary king, “the sufferer’: (TANTALIZE), TANTALUS. 6. Perhaps zero-grade form *tla- in Greek Atlas (stem Atlant-), name of the Titan supporting the world: ATLANTIC, ATLAS. 7. Suffixed zero-grade form *tl-é- in Germanic *thulén in Old English tholian, to suffer, endure: THOLE. 8. Suf- fixed zero-grade form *tl-to- in Latin ldtus, “carried, borne,” used as the suppletive past participle of ferre, to bear (see bher-'), with its compounds: ABLATION, COL- LATE, DILATORY, ELATE, ILLATION, LEGISLATOR, OB- LATE], PRELATE, PROLATE, RELATE, SUPERLATIVE, TRANSLATE. 9. Suffixed zero-grade form *tl-d- in San- skrit tuld, scales, balance, weight: TAEL, TOLA. 10. Nasal- ized zero-grade form *tl-n-a- in Latin tollere, to lift: EXTOL. [Pok. 1. éel- 1060.] tem-. Also teme-. To cut. I. Form *tema-. Nasalized form *t(e)m-n-a- in Greek temnein, to cut: TMESIS, TOME, -TOME, -TOMY; ANATOMY, ATOM, DIATOM, DICHOTOMY, ENTOMO-, EPITOME. II. Form *tem-. 1. Suffixed form *tem-lo- in Latin templum, temple, shrine, open place for observation (augury term < “place reserved or cut out”), small piece of timber: TEMPLE!, TEMPLE’; CONTEMPLATE. 2. Extended root *tem-d- becoming *tend- in o-grade suffixed (iterative) form *tond-eyo- in Latin tondére, to shear, shave: TONSURE. [Pok. 1. tem-, tend- 1062.] teme-. Dark. Suffixed form *tema-s-. 1. Latin temere, blindly, rashly: TEMERARIOUS, TEMERITY. 2. Suffixed form *temas-rd- in Latin tenebrae (plural), darkness: TENEBRAE, TENEBRIONID. [Pok. tem()- 1063.] temp-. To stretch. Extension of ten-. 1. Possibly Latin tempus, temple of the head (? where the skin is stretched from behind the eye to the ear): TEMPLE?. 2. Zero-grade form *tmp- perhaps in: a. Persian taftan, to weave (the
ten-
warp threads are stretched on the loom): TAFFETA; b. Iranian *tap-, “carpet,” in Greek tapés, carpet: TAPES- TRY. [Pok. temp- 1064.] ten-. To stretch. I. Derivatives with the basic meaning. 1. Suffixed form “ten-do- in: a. Latin tendere, to stretch, extend: TEND!, TENDER?, TENDON, TENSE!, TENT!; AT- TEND, CONTEND, DETENT, DISTEND, EXTEND, INTEND, OSTENSIBLE, PRETEND, SUBTEND; b. Latin portendere, “to stretch out before” (por-, variant of pro-, before; see per’), a technical term in augury, “to indicate, presage, foretell”: PORTEND. 2. Suffixed form *ten-yo- in Greek teinein, to stretch: TENESMUS; BRONCHIECTASIS, EPITA- SIS, HYPOTENUSE, PERITONEUM, PROTASIS, TELANGIEC- TASIA. 3. Suffixed zero-grade form *tn-nu- in Sanskrit tandéti, he stretches or weaves, with suffixed (instrumen- tal) derivative *ten-tro- in tantam, loom: TANTRA. 4. Suf- fixed form *ten-tro- in Persian ¢tdr, string: SITAR. 5. Basic form (with stative suffix) *ten-é- in Latin ten� �re, to hold, keep, maintain (< “to cause to endure or con- tinue, hold on to”): TENABLE, TENACIOUS, TENACULUM, TENANT, TENEMENT, TENET, TENON, TENOR, TENURE, TENUTO; ABSTAIN, CONTAIN, CONTINUE, DETAIN, ENTER- TAIN, LIEUTENANT, MAINTAIN, OBTAIN, PERTAIN, PERTI- NACIOUS, RETAIN, (RETINACULUM), SUSTAIN. II. Derivatives meaning ‘‘stretched,” hence “thin.” 1. Suffixed zero-grade form *tn-u- in Germanic *thunw-, whence *thunniz in Old English thynne, thin: THIN. 2. Suffixed full-grade form *ten-u- in Latin tenuis, thin, rare, fine: TENUOUS; ATTENUATE, EXTENUATE. 3. Suf- fixed full-grade form *ten-ero- in Latin tener, tender, delicate: TENDER!, TENDRIL. III. Derivatives meaning “something stretched or capable of being stretched, a string.” 1. Suffixed form *ten-dn- in Greek tenén, ten- don: TENO-. 2. Suffixed o-grade form *ton-o- in Greek tonos, string, hence sound, pitch: TONE; TONOPLAST. 3. Suffixed zero-grade form *tn-ya- in Greek tainia, band, ribbon: TAENIA; POLYTENE. [Pok. 1. ten- 1065.] teng-. To soak. 1. Latin tingere, to moisten, soak, dye: TAINT, TINCT, TINGE, TINT; INTINCTION, STAIN. 2. Zero-grade form *tng- in Germanic *thunk- in Old High German thunk6n, dunk6n, to soak: punk. [Pok. 1. teng- 1067.] tenk-'. To stretch. Extension of ten-. Perhaps Germanic *thingam in: a. Old English thing, assembly, (legal) case, thing: THING; b. Old Norse thing, assembly: HUSTINGS; c. Old High German thing, ding (> German Ding), thing: DINGUS. [Pok. 1. tenk- 1067.] tenk-2, To become firm, curdle, thicken. 1. Suffixed form *tenk-to-, thickened, in Germanic *thinhtaz in Old Norse théttr, dense, watertight, akin to the Scandinavian source of Middle English thight, dense: TIGHT. 2. Possibly suffixed o-grade form *tonk-lo- in Germanic *thangul- in Old Norse théngull, seaweed (? < “thick mass”), akin to the source of TANGLE?. [Pok. 2. tenk- 1068.] tens-. To stretch, draw. Extension of ten-. Suffixed zero-grade form *tns-ero- in Sanskrit tasaram, shuttle: TussAH. [Pok. tens- 1068.] tep-. To be warm. Suffixed (stative) form *tep-é- in Latin tepére, to be warm: TEPID. [Pok. tep- 1069.] ter-. Base of derivatives meaning peg, post, boundary marker, goal. 1. + This Proto-Indo-European entry contains reconstructed terms and roots . As such, the term(s) in this entry are not directly attested , but are hypothesized to have existed based on comparative evidence.
+ to cross over , pass through , overcome
+ Terms derived from the Proto-Indo-European root *terh₂- (95 c, 0 e)
+ Proto-Indo-Iranian: *tárHati ( see there for further descendants )
+ Proto-Indo-Iranian: *títarHti ( see there for further descendants )
+ Proto-Celtic: *taryeti ( “ to burst, spring forth ” ) ( see there for further descendants )
+ Vedic Sanskrit: तूर्य ( tūrya , “ to conquer ” , 2sg.impv. )
+ ⇒ Latin: intrō ( “ to enter, go into, penetrate ” ) ( see there for further descendants )
+ ⇒ Ancient Greek: ἀτέραμνος ( atéramnos , “ hard, stubborn, merciless ” )
+ Proto-Celtic: *trātu ( see there for further descendants )
+ ⇒ Sanskrit: दुष्तरीतु ( duṣtárītu , “ difficult to be passed or overcome ” ) ( + दुस्- ( dus- , “ difficult ” ) )

+ From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] ( cʾp̄wk' /⁠čābuk⁠/ , “ agile, nimble; excellent ” ) , Northern Luri چںڤوک ( çəvok ) , suffixed from an unattested root borrowed as Old Armenian ճեպ ( čep , “ haste ” ) . Akin to Old Armenian ճապուկ ( čapuk ) , Old Georgian ჭაპუკი ( č̣aṗuḳi ) , ჭაბუკი ( č̣abuḳi ) , Middle Iranian borrowings.
+ چابک • ( čâbok ) ( comparative چابک‌تَر , superlative چابک‌تَرین )
+ → Ottoman Turkish: چابوق ( çabuk ) , چاپوق ( çapuk ) , چابك ( çabük ) , چاپك ( çapük ) , چاپوك ( çapük ) , چویك ( çevik )
+ → English: chabuk , chabouk , chaubac , chaubuck , chawbuck
+ → English: sjambok , sambock , sambok , shambock , shambok , shambuck , sjambock , shambock , shambok , sjambock , sjamboke

test,  n.,  a  cupel  for  refining  or  trying  metals; examination,  trial.  —  ME.,  fr.  MF.,  fr.  OF.,  fr.
L.  testu,  testum,  "vessel,  earthen  vessel,  pot', which  is  rel.  to  testa,  ‘piece  of  burnt  clay,  pot¬ sherd,  shell,  scale",  and  prob.  cogn.  with  Avestic tashta-,  ‘cup",  Lith.  list  as,  ‘vessel  made  of  willow twigs",  and  with  L.  texere,  ‘to  weave",  fr.  I.-E. base  *tekth-,  'to  weave".  See  text  and  cp.  testudo. Cp.  also  tester,  ‘canopy".
Derivatives;  test,  tr.  v.,  to  refine  in  a  cupel;  to put  to  the  test;  to  try,  examine,  testable  (q.v.), tester  (q.v.),  test-ing,  adj.,  test-ing-ly,  adv. test,  n.,  the  hard  shell  of  many  invertebrates  ( zoal .) —  L.  testa,  ‘shell’.  See  test,  ‘cupel’, testable,  adj.,  capable  of  being  tested.  —  Formed with  suff.  -able  fr.  test,  ‘to  try".  See  test,  ‘cupel’, testable,  adj.,  capable  of  being  disposed  of  by will  (law.)  —  L.  testabilis,  ‘that  has  a  right  to give  testimony",  fr.  testdri.  See  testament  and -able.
Testacea,  n.  pi.,  an  order  of  invertebrates  covered with  shells.  ( zoo! .)  —  ModL.,  fr.  L.  testaceus, ‘covered  with  a  shell".  See  testaceous, testacean,  adj.,  any  of  the  Testacea.  —  See  prec. word  and  -an.
text,  n.  —  ME.,  fr.  MF.  (=  F.)  texte,  fr.  OF.,  fr. L.  textus,  ‘texture,  structure;  context’,  from  tex- tus,  pp.  of  texere,  ‘to  weave,  plait,  fit  together’, which  is  cogn.  with  OI.  tdkgati,  ‘he  fashions, constructs’,  taksan,  ‘carpenter’,  Avestic  task-,  ‘to cut,  carve’,  tasha,  ‘ax,  hatchet’,  Gk.  xbcxov, ‘carpenter’,  xsyvr,  (for  *teks-nd-),  ‘art’,  OSlav. tesla,  ‘ax,  hatchet’,  tesp,  tesati,  ‘to  hew,  fell,  cut down’,  tesu,  ‘beam’,  Lith.  taiau,  taSyti,  ‘to  cut, carve’,  OIr.  tal  (for  *tdkslo-),  ‘cooper’s  ax,  ma¬ son’s  ax',  Arm.  t‘ek‘em,  ‘I  turn,  wind,  twist’, OHG.,  MHG.  dahs,  G.  Dachs,  Du.  das,  ‘badger’
[ML.  taxus,  taxo,  It.  tasso,  F.  taisson,  Sp. texon  (now  spelled  tejdri),  ‘badger’,  are  Teut. loan  words],  lit.  ‘the  builder’,  ON.  pattr,  ‘thread, wick’.  Cp.  also  Hitt,  taksh-,  ‘to  join,  unite, build’,  takshan,  ‘together’.  All  these  words  de¬ rive  fr.  I.-E.  base  *tekht-,  *tekh-,  ‘to  build  (of wood),  carpenter;  to  weave’.  The  original  mean¬ ing  of  this  base  prob.  was  ‘to  plait,  twist’.  Cp. architect,  context,  dachshund,  pretext,  subtle, Taxidea,  technic,  tecto-,  ‘builder’,  Tectona,  tec¬ tonic,  tela,  telary,  tessitura,  test,  ‘cupel’,  textile, thixle,  tiller,  tissue,  toil,  ‘net’.
textile,  adj.  —  L.  textilis,  ‘woven’,  fr.  textus,  pp. of  texere.  See  text  and  suff.  -ile.
Derivative:  textile,  n.
textlet,  n.,  a  little  text.  —  Formed  fr.  text  with the  dimin.  suff.  -let.

lines: + From Middle Persian [script needed] ( syc /⁠sēj⁠/ , “ danger, trouble ” ) , compare Avestan 𐬌𐬚𐬌𐬌𐬈𐬘𐬀𐬵 ( i θiiejah ) .
+ سیج • ( sēj / sij ) ( plural سیج‌ها ( sēj-hā / sij-hâ ) , Tajik spelling сеҷ )
+ Synonyms: سختی ( saxtī  / saxti ) , محنت ( mihnat  / mehnat ) , مشقت ( mašaqqat  / mašaġġat ) , رنج ( ranj )
+ Steingass, Francis Joseph ( 1892 ), “ سیج ”, in A Comprehensive Persian–English dictionary (overall work in English), London: Routledge & K. Paul
+ Dehkhoda, Ali-Akbar ( 1931– ), “ سیج ”, in Dehkhoda Dictionary Institute , editors, Dehkhoda Dictionary (in Persian), Tehran: University of Tehran Press .
+ MacKenzie, D. N. ( 1971 ), “sēj”, in A concise Pahlavi dictionary , London, New York, Toronto: Oxford University Press, page 74
+ Inherited from Prakrit 𑀲𑁂𑀚𑁆𑀚𑀸 ( sĕjjā ) , from Sanskrit शय्या ( śayyā ) , from शी ( śī ) + -या ( -yā ) .
+ سیج • ( sej )  f ( Gurmukhi spelling ਸੇਜ )
+ a soft or decorated bed ( for a couple on a wedding day )
+ Iqbal, Salah ud-Din ( 2002 ), “ سیج ”, in vaḍḍī panjābī lughat (in Punjabi), Lahore: عزیز پبلشرز [ ʻazīz pabliśarz ], page 1842
+ “ سیج ”, in Oxford Punjabi Dictionaries , India: Oxford University Press, 2022
+ “ ਸੇਜ ”, in Punjabi-English Dictionary , Patiala: Punjabi University , 2026
+ Turner, Ralph Lilley ( 1969–1985 ), “ śēyyā ”, in A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages , London: Oxford University Press, page 731

=== 97b710c758c5031b
 Shortening of طَسْت ( ṭast ) , from Middle Persian tšt' ( tašt ) , ultimately from the past participle of the Proto-Iranian verb *taš- ( “ to make, construct; to cut ” ) , from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tā́ćšti , from Proto-Indo-European *tḗtḱ-ti ~ *tétḱ-n̥ti , from *tetḱ- ( “ to create ” ) . Doublet of طَشْت ( ṭašt ) and طَسْت ( ṭast ) .
--
 Borrowed from Arabic طَاس ( ṭās , “ bowl, cup ” ) .

 one of the nine chief magistrates of ancient Athens, 1650s, from Greek arkhon "ruler, commander, chief, captain," noun use of present participle of arkhein "be the first," thence "to begin, begin from or with, make preparation for;" also "to rule, lead the way, govern, rule over, be leader of," a word of uncertain origin.

e0nodes.append(N(6,"Avestan","traš 2, trâš 2","disputed",
 "No Avestan verb traš-/trāš- 'to cut' is attested. Nourai's form comes from Abolghasemi (FFD p.46), who reconstructs an Old Iranian (not Avestan) root *traš- with vṛddhi *trāš-a- and a Parthian trāš, and does not link it to PIE *teks-. The only Avestan look-alike is θwarəs- 'to cut, hew' (Vd 5.1 avi dim θwarəsaiti). Cheung calls it isolated in Iranian, and it cannot give tarāš- (Av. θw- gives NP t-, but the vowel and sibilant do not match). Modern scholarship (Cheung 2007 s.v. *taš; Wiktionary تراشیدن) derives NP tarāšīdan/tarāš- from MP tāšīdan 'to cut, cleave' (root *taš- < PIE *tetḱ-), with an intrusive -r- from xarāšīdan 'to scratch'. e2nodes.append(N(1,"Avestan","ithyajah, ithyejah","plausible",
 "Avestan iθyajah-, iθyejah- n. (OAv. Y 34.8; YAv. Vd, Yt) is a real word with an epenthetic i-, < *θyaj-ah-, the exact match of Sanskrit tyájas- n. (< PIE *tyégʷ-os). Bartholomae and Walde-Pokorny gloss it 'Not, Gefahr' ('need, danger'). Pokorny's 'Verlassenheit' ('abandonment') is really the gloss of Sanskrit tyajas, though Cheung also renders the Avestan word 'abandonment (?)'. Nourai's gloss is therefore defensible but not the usual one. The link to PIE *tyegʷ- is standard (Pokorny 1086, Wiktionary), but Cheung (*θi̯aǰ, pp.392-393) warns that 'it is uncertain whether all these Ir. forms are related' to Skt tyaj.",
 "اوستایی iθyajah-/iθyejah- (با i- افزودهٔ آغازین) واژه‌ای واقعی و برابر دقیق سنسکریت tyajas- است، از ریشهٔ هندواروپایی *tyegʷ-. بارتولومه و والده‌ـپوکورنی معنای آن را «تنگنا، خطر» می‌دانند. «رهاشدگی» که نورایی آورده در اصل معنای واژهٔ سنسکریت است، هرچند چونگ نیز با تردید «رهاکردن» را پیشنهاد می‌کند. پیوند با ریشهٔ *tyegʷ- پذیرفته است، اما چونگ دربارهٔ هم‌ریشگی همهٔ صورت‌های ایرانی تردید دارد. پس ادعا با احتیاط پذیرفتنی است.",

e0nodes.append(N(6,"Avestan","traš 2, trâš 2","disputed",
 "No Avestan verb traš-/trāš- 'to cut' is attested. Nourai's form comes from Abolghasemi (FFD p.46), who reconstructs an Old Iranian (not Avestan) root *traš- with vṛddhi *trāš-a- and a Parthian trāš, and does not link it to PIE *teks-. The only Avestan look-alike is θwarəs- 'to cut, hew' (Vd 5.1 avi dim θwarəsaiti). Cheung calls it isolated in Iranian, and it cannot give tarāš- (Av. θw- gives NP t-, but the vowel and sibilant do not match). Modern scholarship (Cheung 2007 s.v. *taš; Wiktionary تراشیدن) derives NP tarāšīdan/tarāš- from MP tāšīdan 'to cut, cleave' (root *taš- < PIE *tetḱ-), with an intrusive -r- from xarāšīdan 'to scratch'. So the root is right but this Avestan intermediate does not exist.",
 "در اوستا فعلی به صورت traš-/trāš- «بریدن» ثبت نشده است. نورایی این صورت را از ابوالقاسمی (فعل‌های فارسی دری، ص ۴۶) گرفته، که آن را ریشه‌ای ایرانی باستانِ بازسازی‌شده (*traš و صورت بالاندهٔ *trāš-a-) و صورت پارتی trāš می‌داند، نه اوستایی، و آن را به teks- هندواروپایی پیوند نمی‌دهد. اوستایی θwarəs- «بریدن» ریشه‌ای جداست که چونگ آن را بی‌همتا می‌خواند. پژوهش امروزی (چونگ، ویکی‌واژه) «تراشیدن» را از فارسی میانه tāšīdan و ریشهٔ *taš- می‌داند و r آن را افزوده‌ای از «خراشیدن» می‌شمارد. پس ریشه درست است، ولی این گرهٔ اوستایی پذیرفتنی نیست.",
 [W+"تراشیدن"],
 [{"ref":"FFD:46","status":"partial","note":"Abolghasemi p.46 (PDF p.51, read from image; saved ocr/FFD/46.vision.txt + 46.png): «تراش ← پهلوی اشکانی trāš ← ایرانی باستان *trāš-a ... trāš صورت بالاندهٔ ریشهٔ traš است. traš و trāš هر دو «بریدن» معنی می‌دهند». The forms and the meaning match the chart, but they are labelled Old Iranian/Parthian, not Avestan, and are not tied to PIE teks-."},
  {"ref":"MON:1060","status":"partial","note":"Mo'in s.v. تراشیدن (MON_part1.txt line 39589): 'ستردن موی به وسیلهٔ تیغ از بدن، خراشیدن و پاک کردن چیزی، رنده کردن ...'. The meaning is confirmed, but the online/OCR text has no Avestan form (the Latin-script Pahlavi tags of the print edition are lost in the OCR)."}],
 [{"src":"CHEUNG","where":"pp.384-385 s.v. *taš (line 25072ff.)","stance":"contradicts","note":"'NP tarāšīdan/tarāš- to shave ... The intrusion of -r- in NP tarāšīdan/tarāš- points to contamination with NP xarāšīdan/xarāš- to scratch (a wound), v. *xrā̆š'. The root is *taš-, not *traš-."},
  {"src":"CHEUNG","where":"p.400 s.v. *θwarš (line 25985)","stance":"contradicts","note":"'Av. θβarəs- is isolated in Iranian: no other correspondences are attested'."},
  {"src":"BRT","where":"col. 645 s.v. taš- (Vd 5.1)","stance":"silent","note":"In the cited passage 'avi dim θwarəsaiti avi dim tāšti' the cutting verbs are θwarəs- and taš-; Bartholomae has no traš-/trāš-."},

e0nodes.append(N(7,"Persian","tarâšîdan","plausible",
 "NP tarāšīdan, present stem tarāš- 'to shave, scrape, whittle' (with an analogical past stem 'tarāšīd', as FFD notes) is accepted as a reflex of the *taš-/*tetḱ- root: MP tāšīdan, tāš- 'to cut, cleave' (MacKenzie p.82) < Proto-Iranian *tā́šti, with an -r- taken over from the near-synonym xarāšīdan 'to scratch' (Cheung 2007; Wiktionary). It is cognate with Northern Luri tāšnyı 'to cut' and Kurdish tāšīn 'to hew, shave'. The root assignment is right, but the chart's route through an Avestan *traš-/trāš- (node #6) is not supported (see #6), hence 'plausible'.",
 "«تراشیدن» (مادهٔ مضارع «تراش»؛ مادهٔ ماضی «تراشید» جعلی و ساخته از مادهٔ مضارع است) از فارسی میانه tāšīdan «بریدن، شکافتن» و ریشهٔ ایرانی باستان *taš- (هندواروپایی *tetḱ-) است. r میانی آن به گمان چونگ از هم‌آمیزی با «خراشیدن» آمده است. پس هم‌ریشگی با «تیشه، تشت» و یونانی tekhnē پذیرفتنی است، ولی گذر از صورتی اوستایی به نام traš/trāš که نورایی آورده تأیید نمی‌شود. ادعا با احتیاط پذیرفتنی است.",

 [{"ref":"FFD:46","status":"supports","note":"FFD p.46: «تراشیدن: «تراشید» مادهٔ ماضی جعلی است، از مادهٔ مضارع ساخته شده است. تراش ← پهلوی اشکانی trāš ← ایرانی باستان *trāš-a» (ocr/FFD/46.vision.txt). It supports Nourai's arrow from traš/trāš, but that intermediate is Abolghasemi's own reconstruction."}],
 [{"src":"CHEUNG","where":"p.385 s.v. *taš","stance":"partial","note":"Same root (*taš, PIE *tetK-, Pok. 1058), with the -r- explained as contamination from xarāšīdan."},
  {"src":"PHD","where":"p.82","stance":"partial","note":"'tāšīdan, tāš- [t'š-ytn'] cut, cleave; create'. There is no MP *tarāš-."},
  {"src":"HRN","where":"no. 387 / Pahlavi no. 200","stance":"silent","note":"Horn lists phlv. tāšītan 'zimmern' (no. 200, p.294) but no NP tarāšīdan entry was found."},

I verified page 509 (book page 479) and wrote `/home/sfmqrb/git/rishe-private/data/verification/page-509.json`. JSON validates and `verify_check.py 509` shows 17/17 nodes verified and 0 PROBLEM lines.

**Verdicts:**
- **Roots (2):** Tex/Teks is confirmed. Tiegu is plausible: Nourai's gloss "to approach shyly" mistranslates Pokorny's "retreat in fear".
- **Nodes (17):** 11 confirmed, 4 plausible, 2 disputed, 0 transcription_suspect.

**Disputed:**
- **Tex #2, Persian tîšeh; taxteh; tašt; tâs.** taxteh comes from MP taxtag, built on taxt "throne", so it is not from *taš-. The past participle *taš-ta- gives tašt, not taxt. tîšeh is only plausible: no MP form is recorded, and Horn puts it with tēz "sharp". tašt and tâs are confirmed.
- **Tex #6, Avestan traš 2, trâš 2.** No such Avestan verb exists. The form is Abolghasemi's (FFD p.46) reconstructed Old Iranian *traš/*trāš (with a Parthian trāš), not Avestan. Cheung and Wiktionary derive tarāšīdan from MP tāšīdan (root *taš-), with an -r- borrowed from xarāšīdan. Because of this, #7 tarâšîdan is only plausible: the root is right, the route is not.

**Other plausible nodes:** Latin testum and English test (#13, #14) are tied to *teks- only by Pokorny and Klein; Wiktionary prefers *ters- "dry". Avestan iθyajah-/iθyejah- (Tiegu #1) usually means "need, danger" (Bartholomae), not "abandonment".

**Extraction errors:** none found. I checked the JSON against the chart text but did not compare it with the printed page image.

**Reference notes:**
- SNS:314 could not be read: the archive.org scan jumps from leaf n174 (pp. 312/313) to n175 (pp. 316/317), so pp. 314–315 appear to be missing.
- BQT:1202 confirms سیج, its footnote on سیجمند, and the Ardā Wirāz verse Nourai quotes.
- I saved what I read from the page images to `data/verification/sources/refs/ocr/FFD/46.vision.txt` (with `46.png`) and `ocr/BQT/1202.vision.txt` (with `1202.jpg`), plus the SNS leaves as `ocr/SNS/312-313.jpg` and `316-317.jpg`.
- Etymonline now returns 403. Its architect page was already archived, so I cite it; for the other English words I used the archived Wiktionary pages.
